author: tom
title: Same-game multis explained
dek: Why the price of a same-game multi is lower than the legs multiplied together, and what that means for you.
body:
A same-game multi combines several selections from one match into a single bet, such as a team to win, a player to kick two goals and a total over 160 points. Every leg has to win for the bet to pay. Same-game multis are now among the most popular bets in Australia, and they are also among the most misunderstood.

How the price is built

With a standard multi across different matches, the price is roughly the odds of each leg multiplied together. Two legs at 2.00 each combine to about 4.00.

A same-game multi is different. Because every leg comes from one match, the outcomes are linked. The combined price is therefore calculated by the bookmaker's model, not by simple multiplication.

Why the price is lower

Outcomes in the same match tend to move together. If a team wins by a lot, its key forwards are more likely to have kicked goals, and the total score is more likely to be high. Treating those legs as independent would make the bet look less likely than it really is, so bookmakers lower the combined price to reflect the connection.

LegsOdds if independentTypical same-game price
Team to win (1.80) + forward 2+ goals (2.20)3.96About 3.20
Add total over 160.5 (1.90)7.52About 5.40

The figures are illustrative, but the pattern is consistent: the more closely legs are related, the bigger the gap between the multiplied odds and the price you are offered.

The margin adds up

Each leg carries a bookmaker's margin, and a multi combines them. A same-game multi with four or five legs can carry a margin several times larger than a single bet on the same match. That is why same-game multis are profitable for bookmakers, and why big wins on them are rare.

  • More legs means a bigger potential return, but a much lower chance of winning.
  • Adding a "safe" leg at short odds still lowers your overall chance.
  • One leg failing loses the whole bet, even if the others come in.

Using them sensibly

If you enjoy same-game multis, keep them as a small part of your betting and set the stake you are happy to lose before you build the bet. Fewer legs give you a better chance of seeing a return. Check your monthly activity statement to see what multis actually cost you over time.

The takeaway

A same-game multi is priced lower than the legs multiplied together because the outcomes are linked, and its margin grows with every leg you add. Treat it as a fun, low-stake bet, not a plan to win big.
